parties:
Jinnat Ali (Md)  ----- Petitioner 
Vs 
Md Abdu Bakkar Siddique and others  ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
8. The learned Assistant Judge found the case not barred by limitation, nor bad for defect of parties while allowing the pre-emption. He further found that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance and also by purchase in the case holding. It is held by him that the petitioner being a co-sharer by inheritance has the highest priority to claim pre-emption in preference to others and in support of his view he relied on the decision reported in 34 DLR 180. The learned Senior Assistant Judge further found that the pre-emptee will not be entitled to get any other price except the kobala price as per section 96(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The learned Assistant Judge, however, assessed the development cost at Taka 5388 which was to be deposited within 30 days by the pre-emptor in favour of the pre-emtee. On the other hand, the learned Subordinate Judge while disposing the appeal concurred with the findings of the learned trial Court on the question of defect of party, limitation and pre-emptees claim of some other price other than the price shown in the Kabala under pre-emption. The learned Subordinate Judge, however, considering the evidence on record reduced the development cost from Taka 5388 to 4000. He further, held that the pre-emptee having acquired his right in the case holding on the basis of a Hiba-Bil-Ewaj, Exhibit Ka, his subsequent purchases of case land by the impugned kabalas under pre-emption are protectable under section 96(10) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and ultimately, he allowed the Appeal reversing the judgment and order of the learned Senior Assistant Judge. 

 9. The moot question that arises now in this Rule is as to whether a transfer by way of simple deed of sale made to a person whose interest accrued in the tenancy prior to such transfer on the basis of a deed of Heba-Bil-Ewaj in lieu of Jainamaj, Tajbih, and the Holy Quran is outside the purview of pre-emption as contemplated under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 13. It is true section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 envisages right of pre-emption to three categories of tenants namely, a co-sharer by inheritance, a purchaser and a contiguous land owner of the land transferred upon deposit of the consideration money of the value of the transferred land as stated in the notice under section 89 or in the deed of transfer together with compensation @ 10% of such amount. But this right has been made excepted in sub-section 10 of section 96 to the five classes of transfers which are not open to pre-emption by anyone claiming under section 96.
